description: The Space Weather Preparedness Strategy sets out the nature of the risk to the United Kingdom from severe space weather, the progress made to prepare for it and the priorities for future work. The Department for Business, Innovation and Skills published it on 28 July 2015 as the UK-wide strategy for preparing for and responding to a severe event. It covers the sectors that might be affected, namely electrical power, transport, satellite navigation and timing, telecommunications and central and local government, and how planning is co-ordinated across sectors. Coverage is the UK as of 2015. Format and access: a 40-page PDF of 904 KB, reference BIS/15/457, on GOV.UK. Licence: GOV.UK publications are normally under the Open Government Licence; free. Caveats: a 2015 policy paper under a previous government; later risk registers and the 2021 scenarios paper update its assessment. It supports emergency response and resilience planning for space weather across infrastructure sectors. Related catalogue records are the UK National Risk Register 2025 and the UK reasonable worst-case space weather scenarios.
